items.question: A Belgian staffing group uses a Claude step to summarise candidate CVs and interview notes into a structured profile that recruiters read and that is stored in the CRM. A candidate has complained that their profile states they were 'dismissed for misconduct from a previous role'. Nothing in their CV or notes says this; the model fabricated it. The profile has been in the CRM for four months and the candidate has been passed over for two placements in that period. What should the architect do first?

options.A: Regenerate the profile from the original CV and interview notes with the current production configuration, since a fresh summary from the same source documents will not contain the fabrication.
options.B: Append the candidate's correction as a dated comment beneath the existing profile, leaving the original text in place so the record of what recruiters actually saw is preserved for evidence.
options.C: Establish where the fabricated statement now exists and whether it was relied on - the CRM field, the retrieval index, exported shortlists and the two placement decisions - before correcting anything.
options.D: Refer the candidate to the model provider, since the inaccuracy originated in the model's output rather than in any data the staffing group supplied or reviewed.

items.question: A customer invokes the GDPR right to data portability against an organisation running a Claude-based service. Which data does that right most directly reach?

options.A: All personal data the organisation holds about the individual, including inferences, risk scores and internal annotations.
options.B: The prompts and completions from the individual's sessions together with the model configuration and system prompt used to produce them.
options.C: Any personal data the organisation processes on the basis of legitimate interests, provided it is held in electronic form in a live system.
options.D: Personal data the individual provided, processed by automated means on the basis of consent or contract, in a machine-readable format.

items.question: A Norwegian medtech company needs a capability only available in a non-EEA inference region and will send de-identified but re-linkable device telemetry plus clinician free-text notes there. Legal has executed the standard contractual clauses with the provider and has told engineering that the transfer question is closed. The architect is preparing the go-live checklist and has three weeks. What should be done next?

options.A: Assess whether the law and practice of the destination would undermine the protections the clauses promise for this data, and add supplementary measures where it would.
options.B: Proceed to go-live, since the clauses are an approved transfer mechanism and their execution completes the transfer requirement for this data flow.
options.C: Record TLS encryption in transit and provider-side encryption at rest in the transfer file as the supplementary measures, and close the checklist item.
options.D: Obtain a written statement from the provider that it has never received a government access request for data in that region, and treat that statement as the assessment of local law and practice.

items.question: A hospital system has added a Claude assistant that retrieves chart content so clinicians can ask questions in natural language. The electronic health record already logs every direct chart open against the individual clinician. Retrieval through the assistant, however, runs under a single application service account, so the record shows one high-volume identity reading thousands of charts a day. The privacy officer has raised this before the assistant is extended beyond the pilot ward. What should the architect change?

options.A: Keep the service account but store the clinician's name and session start time in each conversation transcript, so access can be correlated back to an individual during an investigation.
options.B: Propagate the end user's identity into the retrieval call and log, per access, which clinician caused which record to be surfaced, so entitlement can be enforced at retrieval time.
options.C: Leave the design as it is, since the assistant only reads and never writes, and read access performed by an application account does not require individual attribution.
options.D: Sample ten percent of assistant retrievals for periodic privacy review, which gives proportionate assurance at a fraction of the cost of logging every retrieval.

items.question: A Portuguese bank is writing the data protection impact assessment for a Claude-based debt collections assistant that contacts customers in arrears. The programme manager has asked what the document must actually contain, having seen previous assessments that were mostly architecture diagrams. Which THREE elements are required content? (Choose THREE.)

options.A: A comparison of the chosen model against competing models on published benchmark leaderboards, with internal latency tests run on the collections prompt set.
options.B: A systematic description of the processing operations and their purposes, including the legitimate interest pursued where the processing relies on one.
options.C: The commercial terms, unit pricing and volume commitments agreed with the model provider, and the internal budget line the collections workload draws on.
options.D: An assessment of the necessity and proportionality of the processing in relation to those purposes, including less intrusive alternatives.
options.E: An assessment of the risks to the rights and freedoms of the individuals affected, together with the measures envisaged to address those risks.

items.question: A support assistant's transcript store is being reviewed against PCI DSS. Which statement correctly describes what may be retained?

options.A: Both the primary account number and the card verification value may be retained provided the transcript store is encrypted at rest with strong, well-managed keys.
options.B: The primary account number may never be stored in any form, while the card verification value may be retained to support dispute handling and chargeback evidence.
options.C: Card verification values must not be retained after authorisation at all; the primary account number may be stored only where it is rendered unreadable and the full control set applies.
options.D: Neither value is in scope once it appears inside a model prompt rather than in a payment form, because prompt payloads are transient application data rather than storage.

items.question: When scoping a SOC 2 engagement for an AI platform, which trust services criteria category is always included, with the others added according to what the report needs to cover?

options.A: Security, which provides the common criteria that every SOC 2 engagement is built on.
options.B: Availability, since continuity of service is the concern that drives most enterprise buyers.
options.C: Confidentiality, since it speaks most directly to how customer data is handled.
options.D: Privacy, since it is the only category that addresses personal information.

items.question: A Spanish municipality is deploying a third-party high-risk AI system that helps allocate social housing support. Its data protection officer has completed and signed a data protection impact assessment and has told the programme board that the AI Act assessment obligations are therefore covered, since both documents examine risk. The architect is asked to confirm before the board signs off. What is the correct position?

options.A: The completed data protection assessment discharges both obligations, since fundamental rights risks are a subset of data protection risks in any processing of personal data.
options.B: Neither assessment is needed by the municipality, because the provider carried out the conformity assessment for the system before placing it on the market.
options.C: The fundamental rights assessment replaces the data protection assessment for public bodies deploying high-risk systems, so the signed document should be withdrawn and reissued in the new form.
options.D: The two assessments have different subject matter and neither substitutes for the other; they may share evidence and run together, but both must be completed and recorded.

items.question: A US insurer's model risk policy requires every model to be entered in the inventory and assigned a tier that sets validation and monitoring intensity. The claims business unit argues that its Claude assistant, which summarises claim files and drafts a recommended reserve range that adjusters then set, should not be registered because it produces text rather than a number and an adjuster always makes the final entry. Model risk has asked the architect to adjudicate. What should the recommendation be?

options.A: Exclude it from the inventory: quantitative methods that produce estimates are models, whereas generative text tools are productivity software governed under technology standards.
options.B: Register and tier it by the influence its output has on the decision and the reliance placed on it, since inclusion turns on decision impact rather than output format.
options.C: Register it automatically at the highest tier, because generative outputs cannot be validated with conventional statistical techniques and therefore carry maximal residual uncertainty.
options.D: Register it only once it begins operating without human review, since the adjuster's final entry keeps the tool outside the model definition until then.

items.question: A bank's independent validation team must validate a Claude-based system that drafts suitability assessments for retail investment advice. To handle the volume, the team proposes grading the system's outputs with the same Claude model acting as a judge, using the rubric and example prompts that the development team already wrote for its own regression suite. The head of validation asks the architect whether this is acceptable.

options.A: It is acceptable, because judging is a different task from generation and a model evaluating output it did not itself produce performs a genuinely separate function.
options.B: It is acceptable provided the validation team documents the judge prompt, the rubric and the sampling method in the validation report, since documented method supplies the independence.
options.C: It is not acceptable as proposed: validation must build its own reference set and test design, and calibrate any automated grader against human judgement it controls.
options.D: It is not acceptable in any form, because automated grading cannot support an independent validation conclusion and the assessment sample must be graded entirely by qualified humans.

items.question: What should determine how long an organisation retains the request and response records of a regulated AI system?

options.A: The longest applicable obligation across regulatory, evidential and contractual needs, with a defined deletion event at the end of it.
options.B: The default retention configured on the observability platform, since consistency across all systems simplifies audit preparation.
options.C: The shortest retention guidance in the organisation's data protection standard that applies to any field in the record.
options.D: The period for which the model provider retains its own copies of the same requests, so that the two align.

items.question: A Danish pension provider runs a Claude assistant that answers member questions about their scheme rules using retrieval over the scheme documentation. The regulator has asked how the provider can explain to a member why they were told what they were told, and has indicated it will test a sample of answers. Two proposals are on the table: capture and store the model's reasoning output for every answer, or enforce grounding and record source provenance. Which should the architect adopt and why?

options.A: Store the model's extended reasoning output with every answer and disclose it on request, since it is the closest available account of how the answer was produced.
options.B: Store the complete rendered prompt and make it available to members who ask, since it contains everything the model was given and therefore everything that could have influenced the answer.
options.C: Have a second model generate a plain-language explanation of the first model's answer and disclose that, since it can be tuned for member comprehension and reading level.
options.D: Enforce grounding and record which source passages the answer was drawn from, so a member or the regulator can check the cited passage against the scheme rules themselves.

items.question: A provider is building a high-risk AI system for the EU market and is separating engineering work from documentation work in its delivery plan. Which THREE requirements must be built into the system itself rather than satisfied by organisational documentation? (Choose THREE.)

options.A: Explicit consent obtained from every person the system's outputs concern before the system may be used on their data.
options.B: Publication of the training dataset so that affected persons and researchers can inspect what the system learned from.
options.C: Automatic recording of events over the system's lifetime, at a granularity that allows its functioning to be traced.
options.D: A design that enables effective human oversight, including the ability for an overseeing person to intervene in or interrupt operation.
options.E: An appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity for the intended purpose, with performance characteristics declared.

items.question: A US school district contracts an edtech vendor whose product uses Claude to generate feedback on student essays. Twelve months in, the vendor proposes retaining the essays and the generated feedback to improve its own models across all its district customers, and asks the district's technology director to approve it by email as a service enhancement. The district's architect is asked to review before the reply is sent.

options.A: Student essays are the students' own work rather than administrative records, so they sit outside the student records framework and the vendor may retain and use them as it wishes.
options.B: The vendor holds these records only to perform the service the district authorised, so cross-customer model improvement is a separate purpose that needs district review and a contract amendment.
options.C: Aggregating essays across districts before training removes them from the framework, since no individual student remains identifiable in the trained model weights.
options.D: The district may authorise the training use unilaterally, because the vendor is performing a service for the district and therefore acts under the district's authority for anything it does with the data.

items.question: A German manufacturer plans to deploy a Claude assistant in its service desk. Alongside answering agent questions, the product team wants a feature that scores each handled ticket for quality from the transcript and rolls the scores up per agent. The operations director's position is that the scores are for coaching only and will never be used in performance reviews, so the rollout can proceed on the normal change calendar. What should the architect raise?

options.A: A system capable of monitoring employee performance or behaviour engages co-determination regardless of stated intent, so works council involvement must be planned into the delivery timeline.
options.B: Because the scores are used for coaching rather than discipline, the deployment falls within managerial prerogative and no prior consultation with the works council is required.
options.C: Reporting the scores only at team level with agent identifiers removed takes the deployment outside the scope of co-determination, since no individual is being monitored.
options.D: Collecting written consent from each agent before enabling the scoring feature is the appropriate route, since individual consent is the strongest available basis in an employment setting.

items.question: A German manufacturer is adding a Claude-based warranty-claim triage feature to its customer portal. The feature introduces a new processing purpose and engages a new processor, and it handles EU customers' personal data. The processing has been assessed and is not likely to result in high risk. Which TWO documentation artefacts must be updated as a direct consequence? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: A data protection impact assessment, which is required whenever a new processor is engaged to handle personal data on the controller's behalf.
options.B: A consent record for each affected customer, because introducing a new processing purpose requires fresh consent before the purpose can be relied on.
options.C: The record of processing activities, extended with the new purpose, the categories of data and recipients, and the retention period.
options.D: A model card setting out the system's evaluation results, which must accompany any AI-assisted processing of personal data.
options.E: The information provided to data subjects, since a new purpose and a new category of recipient change what must be disclosed to customers.

items.question: A Latvian lender must keep a tamper-evident record of every automated credit decision for its supervisory retention period, and also receives erasure requests from declined applicants whose data it no longer needs for any other purpose. The two obligations appear to collide. Which TWO design or process changes resolve the conflict defensibly? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Encrypt the whole sealed record and destroy the key on request, treating key destruction as satisfying erasure in all circumstances without further analysis.
options.B: Keep only the case identifier, model version, outcome and input hashes in the sealed record, and hold the personal-data payload in a separately erasable store that the record references.
options.C: Move the sealed record store to a jurisdiction whose law does not recognise an erasure right, so the conflict does not arise for that copy of the record.
options.D: Shorten the sealed record's retention to the shortest data protection retention guidance applicable to any field it contains, so erasure and retention converge.
options.E: Document the specific obligation that requires the residual record to survive, and tell the individual which of their data is being retained on that basis and why.

items.question: A Swedish HR software vendor processes customer employee data through a Claude-based assistant. Its data processing agreement gives customers thirty days' notice of new subprocessors and a right to object. The platform team wants to add a specialist third-party reranking service that will receive retrieved text fragments containing employee names and case details, to improve answer quality. The team has scheduled it into next sprint's release. What should the architect raise?

options.A: Because the reranker sees only text fragments rather than complete employee records, it is a technical component of the retrieval stack rather than a subprocessor, and the notice process does not apply.
options.B: Notice is required only where the new subprocessor operates from a different country than the existing ones, so the obligation turns on where the reranking service is hosted.
options.C: The reranker is a new subprocessor processing customer personal data, so the notice period and objection right must run before it goes live, and the architecture must be able to operate without it.
options.D: The obligation is met by updating the published subprocessor list on the vendor's website on the day the change is released, since that is how customers are informed of the current chain.

items.question: A UK retailer's Claude assistant answers product questions on its website. Reviewing transcripts, the team finds that customers routinely volunteer health information - 'I need this chair because of my back condition', 'is this suitable for a diabetic diet' - and that the assistant's summariser writes a short interest profile back to the CRM for personalisation. The lawful basis analysis done at launch covered ordinary personal data only. What is the correct assessment?

options.A: No additional condition applies, because the customer volunteered the information unprompted and the retailer neither requested it nor asked any health question.
options.B: The data is not special category in the retailer's hands, because the retailer has no intention of inferring health status and uses the detail only for product relevance.
options.C: Retention in the transcript is incidental processing outside the framework, because the assistant does not act on the health information when it generates its answer to the customer.
options.D: Health details in the transcripts are special category data requiring an additional condition; the options are to establish one or to stop retaining and deriving from them.

items.question: Under GDPR, what must a processor do when it becomes aware of a personal data breach affecting a controller's data?

options.A: Notify the relevant supervisory authority directly within the statutory deadline, acting on the controller's behalf.
options.B: Notify the controller without undue delay, leaving the risk assessment and any onward notification to the controller.
options.C: Assess the likely risk to individuals and notify those individuals directly where that risk is high.
options.D: Notify the controller only where the processor's own assessment concludes the breach is likely to result in a risk to individuals.

items.question: A US health system's platform team keeps its prompt templates in a Git repository that all of engineering can read, that is mirrored into an internal code search tool, and whose CI pipeline prints rendered templates into build logs retained for ninety days. An engineer materially improved discharge-summary quality by adding three few-shot examples copied from real patient charts, with the patient names replaced by initials. The change passed code review and has been live for two months. What is the correct assessment?

options.A: Real clinical content in a template is protected health information across source control, its mirrors, the build logs and every clone; replace the examples with synthetic content and add a CI check.
options.B: The examples are acceptable because prompt templates are configuration rather than clinical data, and the repository is already covered by the organisation's existing information security controls and access reviews.
options.C: The examples are acceptable now that names have been reduced to initials, since removing direct identifiers satisfies the minimum necessary standard for a development artefact of this kind held in source control.
options.D: The exposure is adequately managed by narrowing repository access to the platform team and requiring a second reviewer on any change touching prompt files before it merges.

items.question: A logistics scale-up is closing its largest enterprise deal. The prospect's security questionnaire asks: 'Is your AI platform GDPR certified and SOC 2 compliant?' Sales wants both answered yes so the deal can progress this quarter. The scale-up holds a SOC 2 Type II report scoped to security for its core platform, which does not cover the new Claude-based module. How should the architect answer?

options.A: Answer yes to both and attach the SOC 2 report, since it evidences the security controls that data protection law requires and therefore covers the second question for the new module too.
options.B: Decline to answer until the organisation has obtained formal GDPR certification from the relevant supervisory authority, and tell sales the deal must wait until it is issued.
options.C: State what is held and what it covers - the report's scope and observation period, and that the new module sits outside it - and answer the data protection question by describing measures and roles.
options.D: Answer yes to the SOC 2 question and, for the data protection question, refer the prospect to the model provider's published compliance page, since the provider processes the data on the scale-up's behalf.

items.question: A payments-adjacent SaaS runs a Claude-based dispute-handling workflow on a managed cloud platform, with model inference through the cloud provider's endpoint. Some flows transmit truncated card data and one legacy flow still transmits full account numbers. The assessor has asked how requirements are divided between the SaaS and the cloud provider. The engineering lead's answer is that the cloud provider handles infrastructure security. What should the architect produce?

options.A: The cloud provider's published shared responsibility model, which sets out the division authoritatively and is sufficient documentation for the assessment of this environment.
options.B: The cloud provider's attestation, since a service provider is responsible for every requirement relating to infrastructure it operates and no further documentation is needed from the SaaS.
options.C: A statement that no allocation is needed for most requirements, because the SaaS itself never stores account numbers and only storage triggers assessment responsibility.
options.D: A written responsibility matrix agreed with the provider mapping each applicable requirement to the SaaS, the provider or both, with provider evidence for every inherited control.

items.question: A French ERP vendor is embedding a general-purpose model into a new module that screens supplier invoices for anomalies and recommends payment holds. Its legal counsel's position is that because the model provider bears the obligations attaching to general-purpose models, the ERP vendor inherits a compliant position and needs only to pass through the provider's documentation to customers. What should the architect say?

options.A: Counsel is right for a different reason: since the ERP vendor did not train the model, it holds no obligations under the AI Act at all and its only duties arise under data protection law.
options.B: The ERP vendor has its own obligations for the system it places on the market, determined by what that system is used for; the provider's documentation is an input to those duties, not a discharge of them.
options.C: Both parties owe an identical obligation set for the finished module, which the Act allocates jointly, so either party performing the work satisfies the requirement for both of them.
options.D: The ERP vendor's obligations are determined by the scale of the underlying model, so embedding a smaller general-purpose model reduces the module's obligation set proportionately.

items.question: A Dutch contact-centre operator's product team proposes a feature that infers each caller's emotional state from the live transcript and displays a running frustration score to the agent, with per-agent aggregates shown to supervisors for coaching. The team has drafted a design and asks the architect to review the guardrails, the bias evaluation plan and the human-review step. All employees and callers are in the EU. What should happen next?

options.A: Approve the design to proceed to build with the proposed guardrails and bias evaluation, and classify the feature formally once measured accuracy is available from the pilot.
options.B: Treat it as a high-risk employment system and begin the conformity workstream, since anything producing per-worker measures for supervisors sits in that tier.
options.C: Screen the proposal against the prohibited practices list before any further design work, because emotion inference applied to workers is among the most restricted areas.
options.D: Consult the works council first and let their response determine the design, since employee representation is the binding constraint and the Act governs systems sold externally rather than used internally.

items.question: A Canadian insurer is allocating responsibilities for its Claude-based claims assistant across a three-lines-of-defence structure, and the operating model must be signed off before the system leaves pilot. Which THREE allocations are correct? (Choose THREE.)

options.A: The claims business owner in the first line owns the risk, operates the controls embedded in the process, and performs day-to-day monitoring of output quality.
options.B: Independent model validation is placed in the first line so validators have direct access to the development team's context, tooling and release cadence.
options.C: The third line owns remediation of the control weaknesses it identifies, since it has the clearest understanding of each deficiency it raised.
options.D: The second line sets AI risk policy and standards and independently challenges the first line's risk assessment, control design and monitoring thresholds.
options.E: Internal audit in the third line provides independent assurance over the design and effectiveness of the whole framework, including the second line's own activities.

items.question: A bank's validated Claude-based trade-finance document checker has been live four months. Monitoring covers a weekly automated quality score on a sampled set, input drift, and the rate at which operators override the system. The quality score has been flat. The override rate has fallen from eighteen percent to three percent. Traffic from a newly onboarded commodities business now makes up thirty percent of volume, up from zero. No configured threshold has been breached and the monthly report is green. What should the architect conclude?

options.A: Monitoring is measuring the wrong things: a third of traffic now falls outside the validated population and the collapsing override rate suggests oversight is weakening, so re-validation is needed.
options.B: A flat quality score across a substantially increased and more varied volume is positive evidence that the system generalises, so continuing the current monitoring is the proportionate response.
options.C: The falling override rate shows operators have built appropriate confidence in a system that has proved itself over four months, which is the outcome the deployment was intended to produce.
options.D: The commodities traffic should be added to the sampled quality set at the next quarterly review, which will surface any degradation without disrupting the current monitoring cadence.

items.question: A payments company logs the full rendered prompt, all tool call arguments and the complete completion for every request, in order to reconstruct decisions for its regulator. A security review has found live session tokens and full account numbers in those logs, which are retained for seven years and readable by the platform support rota. The team must fix this without losing the ability to reconstruct a decision. Which THREE changes achieve both? (Choose THREE.)

options.A: Truncate every logged prompt to its first two thousand characters, which bounds both storage growth and the amount of sensitive content retained in the archive.
options.B: Replace credentials, session tokens and API keys in tool call arguments with a reference to the secret's identifier and version, so the log records which credential was used without holding it.
options.C: Store regulated data elements such as account numbers as a token plus a salted hash, so the record can prove which value was used without holding the value.
options.D: Remove the model version and decoding parameters from the log, since configuration metadata gives an attacker useful information about the system's internals.
options.E: Record retrieved document identifiers and content hashes instead of full document bodies, with the bodies resolvable from the versioned corpus on request.

items.question: In a deployment discussion, what distinguishes a data residency requirement from a data sovereignty requirement?

options.A: They are interchangeable descriptions of the same constraint, with sovereignty the term preferred in public sector procurement documents.
options.B: Residency applies to personal data, while sovereignty applies to classified or state-secret material held for government.
options.C: Residency is a contractual commitment made by a supplier, while sovereignty is a technical control implemented by the customer in its own environment.
options.D: Residency constrains where data is stored and processed; sovereignty additionally concerns whose law and which authorities can reach it.

items.question: A UK bank's Claude assistant helps front-line staff answer customer queries during calls, retrieving from a case-notes corpus. That corpus includes notes on accounts under financial crime investigation, including where a suspicious activity report has been submitted. The financial crime team has raised that disclosing the existence of such a report - even indirectly - is an offence. The platform team proposes several mitigations. Which is correct?

options.A: Instruct the model in the system prompt never to mention or allude to financial crime investigations, and add an output filter that blocks the relevant terminology before anything is displayed.
options.B: Allow retrieval of investigation notes but require the agent to confirm their authorisation in the interface before the assistant will surface that content on the call.
options.C: Partition the corpus so investigation content is not retrievable at all in the customer-facing context, enforced by entitlement at retrieval time rather than by any instruction to the model.
options.D: Redact the substance of investigation notes while leaving a placeholder showing that a restricted note exists, so the agent knows to escalate rather than answer the query.

items.question: An aerospace supplier wants a Claude assistant over its engineering documentation so designers can ask questions across drawings, stress reports and test results. Part of that corpus is export-controlled technical data. The platform would run in a multi-region cloud, and the vendor's support organisation - which can access support tooling touching the environment - is staffed across several countries. What should the architect require?

options.A: No additional measures, since the data remains inside the company's own cloud account throughout and the existing identity and access controls already restrict who can read the documents.
options.B: Keep controlled material out of the general assistant, and where it must be included serve it from a deployment with restricted infrastructure locations and support personnel access, evidenced.
options.C: That the documents be marked and users instructed not to paste controlled content into prompts, with periodic reminders and spot checks on the stored transcripts.
options.D: That the corpus be encrypted at rest with company-managed keys, which removes the concern because the content is unreadable to anyone without access to the key material.

items.question: A Brazilian bank wants to tune a model on two years of its own customer service transcripts through its model provider, expecting better handling of local product terminology. The privacy and procurement teams ask what must be settled before any transcript leaves the bank's environment. Which TWO points must be resolved first? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Whether the tuned model will beat prompt engineering on cost and quality per request at the bank's projected volumes.
options.B: Whether the bank's observability retention matches the provider's, so that latency before and after tuning can be compared over the same window.
options.C: Whether the bank has a documented purpose and basis covering the use of customer transcripts for model tuning, distinct from the basis on which the conversations were handled.
options.D: Whether the resulting tuned artefact is available only to the bank, and what happens to both the artefact and the training data at contract end or on termination.
options.E: Whether the original transcripts can be regenerated from the tuned model, since if they cannot the training data ceases to be personal data and no further analysis is needed.

items.question: A global manufacturer is rolling out one Claude-based HR assistant to employees in the EU, the United States, China and Brazil. Legal has produced a matrix showing a local data localisation requirement in one jurisdiction, a collective consultation requirement in another, and a state privacy law elsewhere granting an opt-out from certain automated processing. The programme sponsor wants a single global deployment on one date. Which TWO positions should the architect hold? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Apply the strictest requirement found in any jurisdiction to all of them - localisation everywhere, opt-out everywhere - since a most-restrictive baseline is compliant by construction.
options.B: Design jurisdiction-specific behaviour - data location, retention, feature availability and disclosure text - as per-region configuration rather than a code fork.
options.C: Publish one global privacy notice covering every jurisdiction, since a single document eliminates the risk of inconsistent disclosures between regions and teams.
options.D: Accept that some jurisdictions may need a separate deployment or a later launch where configuration cannot satisfy them, and plan the rollout in waves.
options.E: Route all traffic through the single region with the strongest privacy protections, on the basis that a higher standard automatically satisfies the weaker regimes.

items.question: Which responsibility remains with the controller and cannot be transferred to a processor by contract?

options.A: Accountability for the processing - being able to demonstrate that it complies, including having chosen a processor offering sufficient guarantees.
options.B: Implementing the technical and organisational security measures appropriate to the risk on the systems that hold the data.
options.C: Carrying out the operational steps needed to answer a data subject request against records the processor holds in its own systems.
options.D: Maintaining and updating the record of the processing activities carried out on the data as those activities change.

items.question: A US bank examiner has given a commercial lending team two weeks' notice of a request for twenty-five specific credit files where the Claude-assisted memo system was used, together with evidence that the documented controls operated for each. The system went live nine months ago and no such package has ever been produced. Five separate artefacts are involved - the decision record, the rendered model inputs, the resolved model version, the reviewer's action, and the control evidence - and they live in four different systems. What should the architect do first?

options.A: Export all twenty-five decision records from the log immediately and send them to the examiner, following up with the control evidence as it is gathered over the following days.
options.B: Ask the examiner to reduce the sample to five files, explaining that the system is new and the package has to be assembled manually across four systems.
options.C: Convene model risk, compliance and engineering to agree a response plan and divide the twenty-five files among the three teams to work through in parallel.
options.D: Assemble one complete file end to end across all five artefacts, because doing one reveals which artefact is missing or slow to obtain and whether two weeks is achievable.

items.question: In a RACI for a decision produced by an automated Claude-based system, who or what can legitimately hold the Accountable role?

options.A: The AI governance committee as a body, on the basis that it reviewed the system and approved it into production.
options.B: The vendor supplying the model, under the indemnity and service terms that cover the deployment in question.
options.C: A named individual who can change, pause, or override what the system decides.
options.D: The model itself, provided its system card records the decision criteria and the confidence thresholds applied.

items.question: A Dutch logistics operator with 3,200 staff has been asked by its board for a complete list of AI tools in use. HR circulated a self-declaration form and received twelve declarations. The CISO believes the real figure is far higher. The company issues corporate cards to team leads, runs an identity tenant where third-party application consent is enabled and logged, and retains full egress-proxy records. Which approach produces the most complete picture?

options.A: Re-issue the self-declaration with mandatory line-manager countersignature and a hard deadline, escalating any team that fails to return it to the executive committee for follow-up.
options.B: Query the procurement and vendor-master systems for contracts and purchase orders containing AI or machine-learning terms, on the basis that anything material to the business would have passed through purchasing.
options.C: Block the well-known consumer AI domains at the egress proxy and treat the helpdesk exception requests that follow as the discovery mechanism, since anyone genuinely dependent on a tool will surface themselves within a week.
options.D: Reconcile corporate card and expense line items, third-party application consents in the identity tenant, and egress-proxy destinations against the declared list, then investigate every difference.

items.question: A Norwegian energy utility runs a Claude assistant that drafts outage notifications to customers. Its incident policy defines an incident in terms of service availability. Over six weeks three things happened: a notification naming the wrong substation went to 4,000 customers; a support agent noticed the assistant citing a decommissioned safety procedure and mentioned it in a team channel; and the assistant was unreachable for twenty minutes. Only the twenty-minute outage was raised as an incident. The risk committee asks how the incident definition should change. Which TWO changes address the gap? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Add trigger criteria based on incorrect or harmful output reaching a customer or being relied on for a decision, independent of whether the service was available.
options.B: Require an AI incident to be declared only once the model provider has confirmed a defect, so the utility does not raise incidents for ordinary probabilistic variation in a generative system.
options.C: Give any employee a low-friction route to declare a suspected AI incident, with triage assigning severity afterwards rather than requiring the reporter to establish impact first.
options.D: Collapse the severity scale into a single AI incident category so that every AI event receives an identical response and no triage judgement is required at declaration time.
options.E: Route AI-related events to the monthly model governance forum instead of the incident process, on the basis that generative output problems are quality defects rather than operational failures.

items.question: A German medical-device manufacturer's after-sales function has built a Claude assistant that helps field engineers diagnose equipment faults. The internal standard requires a system card before production. The team submitted the model provider's published model documentation, arguing that capabilities and limitations are already described there. The governance office rejected the submission. What must the system card supply that the provider's documentation cannot?

options.A: A restatement of the provider's published benchmark results, mapped onto the manufacturer's product families so that reviewers can compare the chosen model against the alternatives considered.
options.B: The specifics of this deployment: the tasks it is approved for, the data it can reach, results from evaluation against the manufacturer's own fault cases, and the named owner.
options.C: The underlying model's training-data composition and architecture, which the provider summarises at a high level but does not disclose to the depth a governance card requires.
options.D: A signed attestation from the model provider confirming that the model is fit for diagnostic support in a regulated medical-device setting, countersigned by the manufacturer's quality function.

items.question: An AI policy exception has been granted and entered in the exception register. Beyond the description of what was waived, which single element most determines whether the register remains a control rather than becoming a list of permanent carve-outs?

options.A: An expiry date, after which the exception lapses unless it is re-argued and re-approved.
options.B: The approver's job title and delegated authority limit, with the date on which the waiver was signed off.
options.C: A severity rating derived from the specific policy clause that was waived.
options.D: A hyperlink to the governance forum minutes and the paper tabled when the exception was discussed.

items.question: A UK insurer requires every AI use case to pass a governance review board that meets monthly; median time from submission to decision is eleven weeks. Nine use cases went through the board last year. Internal audit then found twenty-three AI use cases running in production that never did — almost all of them small internal tools built by analysts, such as summarising broker emails or drafting internal meeting notes. The CRO wants the bypass rate down. Which change is most likely to achieve that?

options.A: Make bypassing the board a disciplinary matter: circulate the audit findings to every line manager, require an explanation for each of the twenty-three cases, and reflect repeat bypasses in individual performance objectives.
options.B: Move the board to a fortnightly cadence and add reviewers drawn from each business line so that decision throughput roughly doubles without changing the review criteria.
options.C: Instruct the platform team to refuse any deployment request that does not quote a board approval reference, and withdraw the twenty-three unapproved tools until each has been reviewed.
options.D: Introduce risk tiering with a catalogue of pre-approved patterns: cases that match a documented low-risk pattern self-register and are cleared by the platform team in days, and only cases outside the catalogue reach the board.

items.question: A New Zealand health insurer's member-facing Claude assistant told a member that a treatment was covered when it was not; the member proceeded and the resulting claim was declined. The complaint reached the AI incident channel at 09:10. Prompt templates live in a repository, but production overrides are applied through an operations console that keeps no change history; conversation logs are retained for thirty days. The on-call engineer disabled the assistant with its feature flag at 09:15 and now wants to correct the coverage wording so it can be re-enabled before the afternoon peak. As incident lead, what should happen first?

options.A: Approve the prompt correction and re-enable the assistant before the afternoon peak, then reconstruct the original configuration from the repository's commit history during the postmortem.
options.B: Capture the configuration that was in force during the member's conversation — console overrides, model version, retrieved documents, flag state — and export the affected transcripts before anything is changed.
options.C: Notify the regulator's incident line now, on the basis that a member has suffered financial detriment as a direct result of an automated communication the insurer itself published to them.
options.D: Raise conversation-log retention across the platform from thirty days to seven years, so the evidence supporting this complaint cannot age out during a lengthy dispute.

items.question: A Canadian benefits administrator is onboarding a claims-triage product from a small software vendor. The product is built on a hosted Claude deployment and decides which claims go to a fast-track path and which go to manual assessment. The security team has completed its standard SaaS assessment: independent security attestation reviewed, penetration-test summary read, encryption and single sign-on confirmed, hosting region verified. The AI governance lead says the assessment is incomplete. Which TWO gaps are most material given what this product does? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Whether the contract governs how submitted claim data may be reused — in particular retention and use for improving the vendor's own product — and how those terms flow through to the vendor's model provider.
options.B: Whether the vendor's engineering team uses an AI coding assistant internally, which determines how much of the product's source code was machine-generated and therefore how much of it was reviewed.
options.C: Whether the vendor will notify the administrator and allow re-testing before changing the underlying model or the triage prompts, since the fast-track behaviour can shift with no change on the administrator's side.
options.D: Whether the vendor can produce per-request cost breakdowns so that the administrator can forecast variable spend and hold the contract inside its approved technology budget.
options.E: Whether the vendor's hosting region matches the administrator's primary operating region, so that claim data does not traverse jurisdictions during normal processing.

items.question: An AI risk report is going to a board audit committee whose remit is assurance over the control environment rather than delivery oversight. What should the report lead with?

options.A: Per-system quality metrics for each production deployment, including evaluation pass rates and measured error rates broken down by use case.
options.B: A narrative of the year's AI investment, with spend attributed by business unit and the efficiency savings projected against each programme.
options.C: Coverage and exceptions: how much of the AI estate is registered and assessed, which risk acceptances are open, who owns them, and when they expire.
options.D: An architecture overview of the AI platform showing the gateway, guardrail and logging components and the vendors supplying each of them.

items.question: An Australian state transport agency keeps its AI register in a spreadsheet, updated when a project manager submits a form at design stage. An audit found that 40% of register entries describe systems that were never built or have since been retired, and that three systems currently in production are absent from it. All Claude access within the agency runs through a central gateway that issues per-application credentials. Which change would make the register reliable?

options.A: Require project managers to re-confirm each of their register entries every quarter, with the delivery office chasing non-responses, escalating outstanding ones to the responsible director, and reporting completion rates.
options.B: Move the register out of the spreadsheet into the agency's configuration management database so entries inherit the change-management, ownership and approval workflow already applied to other IT assets.
options.C: Make credential issuance the registration event and reconcile the register against live gateway credentials on a schedule: no credential without an entry, and any credential with no matching entry or no traffic is flagged.
options.D: Shift the registration point from design stage to go-live, so that entries describe systems that actually reached production rather than proposals that may never be funded.

items.question: A Kenyan microfinance lender uses Claude to draft explanations for declined credit applications. Policy requires a loan officer to review and approve each draft before it is sent, and that approval is the lender's accountability record for the decline communication. Officers handle around 180 drafts per shift; the review screen shows the drafted text and an Approve button; median time between opening a draft and approving it is four seconds; the override rate is 0.3%. Internal audit concludes the review is not a control. What is the strongest basis for that conclusion?

options.A: The reviewer is shown neither the applicant's data nor the policy rule behind the decision, and has neither the time nor the information to form an independent view, so the approval records assent rather than judgement.
options.B: The override rate is implausibly low; a review that is genuinely functioning would be expected to disagree with the model on a materially larger share of cases than three in every thousand.
options.C: The approval is recorded against an individual loan officer rather than against the credit committee that owns the decline policy and should therefore own its communication.
options.D: Reviewing every single draft does not scale at 180 per shift; the lender should replace it with a weekly sample sized to a documented confidence level and reported to the operations quality forum, so that officers examine fewer cases properly.

items.question: An organisation issues a blanket prohibition on all use of external AI tools and provides no sanctioned internal alternative. What is the most predictable governance consequence?

options.A: Use continues on personal devices and personal accounts, outside the organisation's logging, contracts and discovery.
options.B: Use falls close to zero, because most staff will not knowingly breach an explicit written prohibition from their employer.
options.C: Vendors begin approaching procurement directly, shifting the organisation's exposure into the contracted and reviewable supply chain.
options.D: Approved projects stall while the policy is clarified, delaying the organisation's technology roadmap by a quarter or more.

items.question: A Singapore property manager runs a Claude assistant for tenants. Today it answers policy questions and drafts replies that a service coordinator reviews and sends. The governance standard requires a fresh risk assessment and re-approval whenever a system's risk profile changes materially. The team proposes several changes for next quarter. Which THREE require re-approval under that standard? (Choose THREE.)

options.A: The assistant will send its replies to tenants directly, with the coordinator reviewing a sample afterwards instead of every message beforehand.
options.B: The assistant will be given a tool that applies rent credits in the billing system up to a fixed per-case limit without a separate approval step.
options.C: The system prompt will be restructured to place the worked examples above the instructions, with the full evaluation suite rerun and the results unchanged.
options.D: Coverage will extend from the residential portfolio to the commercial one, whose lease terms, escalation clauses and dispute process differ and are absent from the current evaluation set.
options.E: Daily request volume is expected to roughly triple as more buildings are onboarded, with the same tasks, the same data sources and the same review step in place.

items.question: What does an AI-specific third-party assessment need to establish that a standard vendor security assessment does not?

options.A: Whether the vendor encrypts customer data in transit and at rest and holds a current independent security attestation covering the service in scope.
options.B: Whether the vendor's availability commitments and support response times are sufficient to meet the buyer's own service obligations to its customers.
options.C: Whether the vendor maintains a documented business continuity and disaster recovery plan that has been tested within the last twelve months.
options.D: How inputs and outputs may be reused, whether the underlying model can change without notice, and how the vendor's own model provider is bound.

items.question: A Polish marketplace ran a postmortem after its Claude-based listing moderation system approved a batch of counterfeit listings that stayed live for nine days. The document correctly traces the cause: the moderation evaluation suite is an optional step in the deployment pipeline, and the prompt change that caused the failure shipped without it. The three actions read: 'be more careful with prompt changes', 'consider adding evals to CI', and 'team to review the moderation policy'. The engineering director signed the postmortem and closed the incident. Which criticism is best supported?

options.A: The postmortem should have been written by a reviewer independent of the team that operates the system, because a team investigating its own failure will understate its contribution to it.
options.B: The postmortem should have identified which engineer approved the merge, so that accountability for the change that caused the exposure is recorded against a named person.
options.C: None of the actions is owned, dated or verifiable, and none makes the evaluation step mandatory, so the condition that produced the failure is still in place at closure.
options.D: Nine days of undetected exposure shows the incident's severity rating was set too low, and the correct remedy is to re-rate it before the incident can be closed.

items.question: A Chilean payments company embeds a third-party dispute-summarisation service in its operations console. Two weeks after a routine vendor release, summaries began omitting the chargeback reason code that the operations team relies on to route cases; the vendor confirmed it had moved to a different model tier. The contract covers security, availability and support but says nothing about model changes. The company's governance standard requires material changes to be assessed before they take effect. Which combination of contractual and operational change addresses this class of failure?

options.A: A contractual requirement that the vendor pin one named model version for the life of the agreement, so the behaviour tested at onboarding is the behaviour that continues to be delivered.
options.B: A change-notification and regression window in the contract — advance notice of model or prompt changes plus time to run the company's own acceptance tests — backed by running that test set against the vendor on a schedule.
options.C: An availability and accuracy service level with financial credits attached to each breach, so that the vendor carries the cost of degraded summaries and has a direct incentive to avoid causing them.
options.D: Rebuild the summarisation in-house on the company's own Claude deployment, retiring the third-party service at the next renewal and giving the operations team direct control over model version, prompt content, release timing and the summary template.

items.question: In a staged rollout of an AI system from pilot to full production, when should the criteria for halting or rolling back be defined?

options.A: After the first stage, once real production data has shown what normal behaviour for this system actually looks like.
options.B: Before the first stage begins, as part of the approval to proceed to that stage.
options.C: At each stage gate, by whichever team is operating the system during that quarter.
options.D: Only if an incident occurs, so that the criteria are grounded in the failure that was actually observed.

items.question: A Brazilian retailer's AI usage policy prohibits placing customer personal data into any AI tool. Enforcement consists of a mandatory annual training module and a signed attestation. Six months on, a data-loss review finds customer records in prompts sent to the sanctioned internal Claude gateway and in traffic to two external consumer AI products. The head of data protection wants enforcement that does not depend on staff remembering the rule. Which TWO changes achieve that? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Apply the existing egress data-loss rules to AI endpoints and to the internal gateway's request bodies, so a prompt carrying customer data is blocked or masked at submission rather than found in a later review.
options.B: Increase the training module from annual to quarterly and add a scored assessment that staff must pass before their gateway credentials are renewed for the following period.
options.C: Route all corporate access to external AI products through the same gateway, or block direct access, so there is a single enforcement point at which the policy can actually be applied.
options.D: Add a full-width warning banner to the gateway interface restating the prohibition and the disciplinary consequences at the start of every session a user opens.
options.E: Require each business unit head to countersign the attestation on behalf of their team, raising the level of management at which the existing commitment is made.

items.question: In an enterprise AI inventory that downstream risk, assurance and reporting processes all draw on, what should the unit of registration be?

options.A: Each model the organisation has approved for use, with the applications that call it listed beneath it.
options.B: Each use case — a defined task, its data, its users and its accountable owner — even where several use cases share one model.
options.C: Each vendor contract under which AI capability is procured, with individual deployments recorded as line items against the master agreement.
options.D: Each application or repository in the software estate, flagged according to whether it makes calls to a model.

items.question: An Irish insurance broker with 900 staff ran a discovery exercise and identified more than sixty unsanctioned AI uses, including several where client data was pasted into consumer products. Legal wants disciplinary action against the individuals identified. The broker's stated objective is a complete and accurate AI inventory within six months, and a sanctioned internal gateway went live last month. Which approach best serves that objective?

options.A: Run a time-boxed amnesty with hands-on migration support onto the new gateway, then enforce technically once the migration path is proven — accepting that the sixty identified cases attract no sanction.
options.B: Take disciplinary action against the identified individuals and publicise the outcomes internally, so that anyone whose use has not yet been discovered understands the consequence of failing to come forward.
options.C: Block the consumer products at the proxy immediately and require a written business case for any exception, working through the resulting requests as they arrive from the affected teams.
options.D: Extend the discovery tooling to cover personal devices on the guest network, so the remaining undisclosed uses can be found without depending on anyone choosing to disclose them.

items.question: A South African bank's Claude-based collections assistant began sending customers settlement figures calculated on a stale balance. Error rates and latency were normal throughout; a collections supervisor noticed the discrepancy at 22:40 on a Saturday. The documented kill switch is a feature flag held in the platform repository: changing it requires a pull request approved by two platform engineers and a pipeline run that averages twenty-five minutes. Neither approver was reachable and the assistant kept sending for three hours. What should the postmortem require?

options.A: Add a third named approver to the flag repository and extend the platform team's on-call rota to cover weekends, so that two approvals are always obtainable within the response target.
options.B: Split flag configuration out of the main deployment into its own lightweight pipeline so the twenty-five minute run drops to under five minutes for a flag-only change.
options.C: Make disabling an operational action the on-call engineer can take alone through a documented, audited runbook step with no code review or deployment, and rehearse it on a schedule.
options.D: Add an automatic circuit breaker that disables the assistant when the error rate crosses a threshold, so that stopping it does not depend on a human noticing and acting at all.

items.question: A Swiss private bank's most recent supervisory return states that it operates four AI systems, none of which make customer-affecting decisions. The internal AI register now lists eleven entries, three of which describe systems that influence client-facing outcomes. The bank's own reporting standard requires every regulatory submission to be reconcilable to the source records that support it. A thematic supervisory review has just been announced. Which TWO actions should the head of compliance take? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Reconcile the return to the register: establish which of the eleven entries fell inside the return's stated definition and which did not, and document the definition that was applied when the return was prepared.
options.B: Reduce the register to the four systems named in the return, so that the bank's two records are consistent with one another before the review team begins its work.
options.C: Correct the submission through the bank's established amendment process if the reconciliation shows the return was wrong, rather than waiting for the review to identify the discrepancy.
options.D: Prepare a briefing note explaining the difference as a matter of interpretation, and hold it in reserve to present only if the review team raises the point directly.
options.E: Suspend the seven systems that were not covered by the return until the thematic review has concluded, so the submission is accurate as at the date of the review.

items.question: An AI governance standard requires that the person who approves a use case into production is not the same person who operates it. Which failure is that separation designed to prevent?

options.A: Knowledge of the system becoming concentrated in one person, so that its continued operation depends on that individual's availability.
options.B: The operating team being held responsible for outcomes that follow directly from decisions the approving body took.
options.C: One individual being able to widen what the system does without any independent party assessing the change.
options.D: Approval decisions being delayed because the person making them is simultaneously carrying a production workload.

items.question: A Mexican utility runs a Claude assistant that answers field technicians' questions about equipment isolation procedures. Over eight weeks the support queue accumulated fourteen tickets whose text says the assistant gave an incorrect isolation procedure. Each was closed individually by an agent who corrected the technician; none was declared an incident, because in every case the technician caught it and no harm occurred. A safety engineer spots the pattern while reading ticket text for an unrelated review. The incident process has no mechanism that aggregates across tickets. What should the safety engineer do next?

options.A: Reopen the fourteen tickets and reclassify each as a low-severity AI incident, so that the volume appears correctly in the next monthly operational report.
options.B: Declare an incident against the aggregate pattern and let triage assess it, rather than leaving fourteen separately resolved tickets as the organisation's only record.
options.C: Raise a defect against the assistant's retrieval index, since incorrect isolation procedures point to stale or superseded procedure documents being returned.
options.D: Propose an amendment to the incident policy requiring any recurring AI-related ticket theme to be declared, and table it at the next governance forum.

items.question: A Finnish media group built a Claude-based archive-tagging system with an external delivery partner. The partner's engagement ended, the internal team that sponsored the work was reorganised, and the register still names a product manager who left eight months ago. The system runs roughly 40,000 tagging calls a week and its output feeds the rights-clearance workflow that determines what the group may licence. Governance has flagged it. What must be established before anything else?

options.A: A support contract with the delivery partner covering defect fixes and model version upgrades for at least the next twelve months of operation.
options.B: A named accountable owner inside the current organisation with the authority and the budget to change, pause or retire the system.
options.C: A refreshed system card recording the current configuration, the evaluation results and the failure modes now known from production use.
options.D: Migration onto the group's standard AI platform so that the system falls under central monitoring, logging and cost attribution.
